answerCheck.reason: A test of independence starts with the null hypothesis that the two categorical variables are independent, then assesses departures from it.
A large departure from the counts expected under independence provides evidence against independence and in favor of association, rather than proving a conclusion.
A contingency-table independence test compares joint category counts with counts expected if the categorical variables were independent.
The statistic sums squared departures from independent expected counts, scaled by those expected counts. A very large total supplies stronger evidence against independence.
